articles.headline: Sources: Steelers to trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys
articles.description: The Steelers agreed to trade cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday night.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：スティーラーズがジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアをカウボーイズへトレード
articles.descriptionJa: スティーラーズがコーナーバックのジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアを2027年のドラフト6巡目指名権および2028年の2巡目指名権との交換でカウボーイズへトレードすることに合意したと、水曜夜に複数の情報筋がESPNに明かしました。
articles.body:
After a lengthy and contentious contract standoff and a lingering back issue, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is going to the Dallas Cowboys.

The Steelers on Wednesday night agreed to trade Porter to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources told ESPN. 

The trade marks the end of a monthslong saga that stretched throughout the Steelers' offseason as Porter, one of the team's 2023 second-round picks, awaited an extension and was sidelined by a back injury.

The heart of the dispute was the guaranteed money within the contract's structure, sources told ESPN, and the sides never made meaningful progress on agreeing to terms despite talks as late as hours before kickoff of the Steelers' Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers then stopped talks because they don't negotiate during the regular season as a longstanding organizational principle.

Porter, who started 41 games and had three interceptions in three seasons, sat out all of the team's training camp and preseason after reporting an aggravation to the back injury during the team's mobility workout on the first day of camp. He was put on the physically unable to perform list until roster cutdown day in late August.

Porter was then a limited participant in every regular-season practice until earlier this week as coach Mike McCarthy said the cornerback was progressing through a "ramp-up" phase during the first month of the season.

Porter was inactive for each of the first three games and had been ruled out earlier Wednesday of the Steelers' game Thursday night against the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers added a back injury to Wednesday's practice report in addition to the "not injury related-conditioning" description the team used for Porter's injury status for most of the past three weeks. Porter had previously been a full participant in the team's Monday and Tuesday walkthroughs.

His departure means the Steelers will continue to operate with Asante Samuel Jr., Jamel Dean and Daylen Everette rotating at outside cornerback. Everette, a 2026 third-round draft pick, played extended snaps in a Week 3 win against the Cincinnati Bengals, first coming in for a briefly injured Dean and then replacing Samuel for much of the second half.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones hinted during training camp that he would be willing to give up draft capital to help this season's team. Jones was asked on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Monday about a potential trade with reports of the team's interest in Porter.

While not specifically talking about Porter because of tampering rules, Jones said, "I'd just say we're right on top of it. We're very aware of the moving parts out here."

articles.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys, J.J. McCarthy to Giants
articles.description: Can Joey Porter Jr. clean up the Cowboys' defense? Will J.J. McCarthy improve the Giants' QB situation? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
articles.headlineJa: NFLトレード期限の移籍評価：ジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアがカウボーイズへ、J・J・マッカーシーがジャイアンツへ
articles.descriptionJa: ジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアはカウボーイズの守備陣を立て直すことができるでしょうか？J・J・マッカーシーはジャイアンツのQB事情を改善できるでしょうか？11月のトレード期限を前に、NFLのトレードを採点・評価します。
articles.body:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, which will pass on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET.

When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here are our evaluations for the first two deals of trading season: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants and Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys. Check back right through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

Steelers trade CB Porter to Cowboys

Cowboys get: CB Joey Porter Jr.

Steelers get: 2027 sixth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Cowboys grade: B

Steelers grade: C+

This is the Cowboys' third trade with the Steelers in the past 18 months (George Pickens and Broderick Jones), and it's their third trade involving a star defensive player after acquiring Quinnen Williams at the trade deadline last season and shipping Micah Parsons to Green Bay last offseason.

It's easy to see what the Cowboys are doing here. DaRon Bland, who first broke onto the scene as a slot corner, was playing on the outside given Dallas' lack of depth. By acquiring Porter, Bland can move back inside, which will allow the Cowboys to relocate 2026 first-round defensive back Caleb Downs, as well. He has been playing the slot, but his natural position is at safety. These are options, not guarantees. Bland might stay outside as the Cowboys instead pursue a strong 1-2 punch at outside corner, with Porter shadowing WR1s.

The salient point is this: Porter can have a rising tide impact on the Cowboys secondary, clarifying the roles of other players and enhancing the whole unit in the process.

Porter is not as tricky of a scheme fit in Dallas as people think, too. His strengths are certainly his length and physicality, such that he can line up in press -- but he has been in press alignments on only 30.6% of his snaps over his career, just above the league average for cornerbacks (24.1%). Porter is a much better man coverage defender than he is in zone, as his passer rating allowed in man coverage over the past four seasons is better than all but Derek Stingley Jr. But the Cowboys are actually running more man coverage (24.8%) under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker than the league average (23.2%) over the first three weeks.

Of course, early-season rate stats can be noisy. Parker's Vic Fangio-inspired defense will require Porter to play from greater depth than he did in Pittsburgh, and the communication and keys required in that match-heavy system will take some getting used to. articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. But the deals have already kicked off.

With quarterback Jaxson Dart undergoing surgery on his left knee last Friday, the Giants traded for Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Amid contract extension negotiations that went nowhere, the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys.

We're tracking all in-season moves and trade-related buzz right through the deadline. Most recent deals will be added at the top.

More coverage:

Transactions | Depth charts

Sept. 30

Steelers trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys

Steelers get: 2027 sixth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Cowboys get: CB Joey Porter Jr.

The Steelers are trading Porter to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round selection, sources confirmed to NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe and ESPN's Todd Archer. 

The trade marks the end of a monthslong saga that stretched throughout the Steelers' offseason as Porter, one of the team's 2023 second-round picks, awaited an extension and was sidelined with a back injury.

Solak: Grading the deal from both sides

Sept. 28

Vikings trade QB McCarthy to Giants

Giants get: QB J.J. McCarthy

Vikings get: 2027 fifth-round pick

The Giants traded for Vikings quarterback McCarthy on Monday, sending a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to Minnesota for the 2024 first-round pick. McCarthy, taken by the Vikings with the No. 10 pick, was the third-string quarterback in Minnesota behind starter Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.

Giants coach John Harbaugh said after their Week 3 victory over the Titans that Jameis Winston would remain the Giants' starter even if the team added another quarterback. He reiterated that Monday after the trade for McCarthy.

articles.headline: Former Steelers HC Mike Tomlin reveals massive Minecraft city
articles.description: The former Steelers coach revealed an unexpected longtime hobby that shocked the sports and gaming worlds.
articles.headlineJa: 元スティーラーズHCのマイク・トムリン、マインクラフトの巨大都市を披露
articles.descriptionJa: 元スティーラーズのヘッドコーチが意外な長年の趣味を明かし、スポーツ界とゲーム界を驚かせました。
articles.body:
Mike Tomlin is a Super Bowl-winning head coach, is second on the Pittsburgh Steelers' all-time wins list and famously never had a losing record in 19 seasons with the Steelers.

But on Wednesday, Tomlin showed a side of himself rarely seen: that of an architect. On Minecraft, to be exact.

Speaking about his passions for high-rise buildings and urban planning, Tomlin unveiled his Minecraft world in a nearly 20-minute YouTube video. Tomlin has been working on the ongoing project for 12-plus years.

After he watched his kids obsessively play the game in middle school, Tomlin became intrigued by the game's creative mode, which allows users to build cities with unlimited resources. The former head coach explains on the video that he likes to build and always had an interest in architecture.

It also became a way for Tomlin to spend time with his kids. Each of them participated and have buildings across the city.

"Over the course of time, they got just disinterested in the game. They go on to high school and so forth and off to college. Their participation became less and less over the years. My participation probably at times increased," Tomlin says, laughing. "At different times over the course of a 12-month calendar, I would have different levels of fixation on this."

He remembers constructing the various communities, neighborhoods and buildings with challenges along the way. But he describes the process of building his world as "mindless entertainment" and "therapeutic."

"I'm not a big TV watcher," he says. "It allowed me to detach from the realities and the pressures of life."

Tomlin shows off the various apartments and architecture, and he gives a tour of buildings, apologizing for his "lack of stick control" with a controller.

He also breaks down his vision for the city: densely populated buildings around a body of water. He started small before building neighborhoods over 12 years.

The first building Tomlin created is a "boutique hotel" that includes an executive spa and therapy rooms. He described himself as "lighting conscious" when building it, using glass ceilings when appropriate. The hotel includes indoor and outdoor boutiques, an elevator well and a main desk.

Another community within his city features an apartment building with an aquarium on each floor.

He says he was "view conscious" of the many high rises, making sure the high-end urban apartment buildings had great sightlines. One of them is right across from baseball and soccer stadiums, which Tomlin teases he'll reveal in another episode.

No detail was too small.

"You'll find appropriate number of public restrooms and stuff throughout all my public facilities, men's and women's restrooms," he says. "Not anything over the top in terms of detail ... but it was important that I represented that."

articles.headline: London game reminds Marcus Mariota of the connection between football and soccer
articles.description: For Mariota, who grew up playing soccer, Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is a chance to combine his love of both sports.
articles.headlineJa: ロンドンでの試合、マーカス・マリオタにアメフトとサッカーのつながりを思い起こさせる
articles.descriptionJa: サッカーをして育ったマリオタにとって、トッテナム・ホットスパー・スタジアムで開催される日曜日のインディアナポリス・コルツ戦は、愛する2つのスポーツへの情熱を結びつける機会となる。
articles.body:
HERTFORDSHIRE, England -- The first sport Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota played as a kid -- soccer -- continues to help him in the one he plays as an adult. But the combination of the two is why Mariota is ecstatic about another opportunity to play in a famed soccer stadium.

There's a strong chance Mariota starts Sunday in place of Jayden Daniels, who was limited in practice Wednesday with a dislocated left elbow. If that happens, then Mariota will have performed a meaningful trifecta for himself: starting football games in three iconic soccer stadiums.

The Commanders (1-2) play the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, home of the team of the same name. Mariota started at the Bernabeu Stadium last season (Real Madrid) and at Wembley, where the England national team plays, in 2019.

In those two games, Mariota lost to the Los Angeles Chargers on a failed two-point conversion at Wembley while playing for the Tennessee Titans; and to the Miami Dolphins in overtime last season. He has a chance to prove that the third time is, indeed, a charm Sunday.

"I grew up being around the game," Mariota said. "So, to play at Wembley and then last year play in Madrid and then now play at Tottenham that's really cool for me. It's kind of a cool moment. So, I'm looking forward to it."

When asked who his favorite Spurs player was, Mariota said former star Harry Kane, the club's all-time leading scorer who left to play with Bayern Munich in 2023.

"I know that might be a little bit rough right now," he said, laughing.

Mariota has been known for his elusive runs, sometimes spinning out of and emerging from harrowing situations in the pocket. And to be a quarterback in the NFL requires having adept footwork.

That's why he said there's a definite connection between the sports.

"Spatial awareness," he said about how soccer helped him. "As you play soccer -- fútbol -- like, you had to know the next move before the ball came to you. And being able to see the field, where people were at, kind of diagnose where to put the ball, I feel like that helped my spatial awareness as a quarterback."

In the pocket, it's also about taking drops.

"All the footwork stuff, definitely," he said. "Whether it's taking five, seven step drops, being out of gun, out of pistol. All those things are little things, but things that I felt like fundamentally soccer brought to me. So, I love the game."

Mariota said he doesn't have a favorite team, but added his brother, Matt, is "religious" about following the English Premier League. Matt Mariota, a former walk-on at Oregon, also played some college football in England at Leeds Carnegie. His team? Liverpool.

The nice thing for Mariota and Washington is that he's coming off a strong performance in a 33-31 win over Seattle, throwing for 176 yards and three touchdown passes.

articles.headline: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey: 'I want to be judged by winning'
articles.description: Coming off a career year, Tyrese Maxey said he doesn't want to be judged by how he does individually but by how the 76ers do as a team this year.
articles.headlineJa: 76ersのガード、タイリース・マクセイ：「勝利によって評価されたい」
articles.descriptionJa: キャリアハイのシーズンを終えたタイリース・マクセイは、今年は個人の成績ではなく、76ersがチームとしてどう戦うかで評価されたいと語った。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Having earned two All-Star nods in the last three seasons and coming off a campaign in which he averaged a career-high 28.3 points per game, Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey is primed for another big year.

But the 25-year-old said Wednesday after the Sixers' second practice of training camp that the only metric he cares about for Philadelphia's highly anticipated upcoming season is team success.

"I'm at the point now where I've showed what I can do talent-wise," Maxey said. "Of course, I'm going to continue to get better, but I want to be judged by winning. If we win, that's what I want to be judged by. That's really my main mindset, my main goal, is finding ways to win."

Maxey was the first of Philly's four major stars -- including Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James -- to speak to reporters since training camp started Tuesday.

Brown sidestepped a query on media day Monday when asked about how the Sixers will determine a pecking order and identify an "alpha" by replying: "Next question."

 

Maxey's answer was in the same spirit, albeit much more elaborate, as he detailed his willingness to adjust to help the team.

"Because I've played so many different roles, I'm capable of doing so many different things," Maxey said. "And I think that's going to be a positive for myself and for this team. I can play on the ball. I can play off the ball. I can play in transition. I can catch and shoot. Play off [of] pin downs. I can play pick-and-roll. ...

"I'm going to play however they need me to play. However Coach [Nick Nurse] wants to play, that's how I'm going to play."

And Maxey is not only leading by example. He is speaking up as the new group gets off the ground.

"My voice carries a little bit and then just the charisma of me smiling and having a good time," Maxey said. "I mean, I'm getting older ... and I just feel like I've been here for a minute. Process [Embiid] has been here, I think what, 13 years? I've been here seven. So, we've been here for a while, kind of know how things go around here and just am trying to keep using my voice and help everybody get familiar and help everybody get comfortable."

Beyond vowing to acquiesce to any role change that is asked of him, Maxey also used his voice to be effusive in his praise of the other stars on the team in his answers Wednesday.

On James: "That's like a big brother to me. He's an old man ... He's a good guy. He's a good guy."

On Embiid: "He looks amazing. He looks happy. ... When you're healthy and you're happy and you're at peace with your life and basketball, that's when you're at your best. He's been great."

On Brown: "JB's like physically a freak of nature. He's just stronger than you. He jumps higher than you. He's faster than you and he's very talented. Those are the things that you see every single day. And I think what's stood out to me so far is his communication and he's willing to pick up the ball defensively, kind of just do whatever coach needs hi

articles.headline: Klopp not preparing for more titles after verdict against Man City
articles.description: Jürgen Klopp said Wednesday he would "wait and see" before commenting on the Premier League's announcement yesterday that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges for breaching financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: クロップ監督、マンCへの有罪判決後もさらなるタイトル獲得の準備はせず
articles.descriptionJa: ユルゲン・クロップ監督は水曜日、マンチェスター・シティが財務ルール違反の114件の違反行為で有罪と認定された昨日のプレミアリーグの発表について、コメントする前に「静観する」と語った。
articles.body:
Jürgen Klopp said Wednesday he would wait to see how things pan out before commenting on the Premier League's announcement yesterday that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges for breaching financial rules.

The charges cover a period between 2009 and 2018, with Klopp's tenure at Liverpool -- which began in 2015 -- overlapping with the time that City were have found to be guilty of breaking Premier League rules.

On the eve of Germany's match against Serbia in the Nations League, though, Klopp seemed content to let his record at Merseyside speak for itself instead of speculating over what might have been.

"I haven't given it much thought, even though I've seen it of course," Klopp said. "Should any sanctions be imposed, I naturally have nothing to do with it anyway, and that's why I'm waiting to see how things pan out. But when you're talking about legal proceedings that have been going on for so long now, I assume there will be an appeal or something like that? That will take ages again of course.

"So I'm a long way from preparing myself for it in any way and I don't have any feelings about it."

City, who won the Premier League three times between 2009 and 2018, have denied all of the charges and are set to lodge an appeal against the verdict.

Of his longtime rival and Man City coach Pep Guardiola, Klopp said:  "I also know what I said about it in the past and how if there's ever a parade, I'll be there. But it doesn't feel like that anymore. My respect for Pep Guardiola and the football played at City during the time we played against each other, in the way they played back then and how they brought football to life on the pitch -- plus what an opponent they proved to be for us at the very highest level -- is far too great for me to be able to say anything now."

Klopp was also tight-lipped on Germany's captain for the Nations League tie -- his third match in charge of the national team. The new Germany coach has a completely new squad to work with after he selected two groups for the four fixtures during this international window.

With regular captain Joshua Kimmich allowed to leave the camp after he featured in a 1-1 draw in the Netherlands and the shock home loss to Greece, Klopp must decide who wears the armband for this clash in Munich.

"The team will be led onto the pitch tomorrow by the player with the most international caps," Klopp said on Wednesday.

Captain question aside, Klopp did hint that Bayern Munich goalkeeper Jonas Urbig would play at his home stadium of Allianz Arena.

"Feel free to ask 'who might be a captaincy option,' but I don't reveal the starting lineup now. You can look them up yourselves," said Klopp. "I can only say that Jonas Urbig won't wear the armband in his first international match."

Urbig took part in a news conference after Klopp and expressed his delight at making his Germany debut.

articles.descriptionJa: ハリー・ケインは、チェコ戦の勝利で存在感を示したラ・リーガ所属の2人について、イングランドの「違いを生み出す選手」アンソニー・ゴードンと代表復帰を果たしたスターのトレント・アレクサンダー＝アーノルドを絶賛した。

articles.headline: Raphinha returns to Barcelona after injury on Brazil duty
articles.description: Raphinha will return to Barcelona after suffering a thigh injury in Brazil's 4-2 friendly win over Australia on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: ハフィーニャ、ブラジル代表活動での負傷によりバルセロナに復帰
articles.descriptionJa: ハフィーニャは火曜日に行われブラジルが4-2で勝利したオーストラリアとの親善試合で太ももを負傷し、バルセロナへ戻ることになった。
